levels.label: unknown
levels.evidence: Objects are not registered anywhere; existence is implicit in paper or operator knowledge.

levels.label: anonymously known
levels.evidence: Objects are counted or tracked by type, lot or batch (e.g. 'profile article X, batch 123'), not per piece.

levels.label: individually known
levels.evidence: Each instance carries a unique ID (serial, DMC, RFID, asset tag) that systems can read and reference.

levels.label: managed as an entity
levels.evidence: Each instance has a managed digital record (state, history, relationships) - an asset or product twin, e.g. an Asset Administration Shell or an entry in a governed asset registry.

levels.label: none
levels.evidence: Isolated machine; data only via manual reading or local display.

levels.label: passive
levels.evidence: Data available only when an external system polls registers or tags (e.g. classic PLC polling, file drops).

levels.label: active
levels.evidence: The asset pushes values or events on change (e.g. OPC UA subscriptions, MQTT publishing).

levels.label: compliant to the service system
levels.evidence: The asset exposes and consumes defined services with contracts (e.g. OPC UA companion-spec methods, Sparkplug-style birth/death and state, standardized command interfaces).

levels.label: none
levels.evidence: No processing.

levels.label: data handling
levels.evidence: Buffers, filters or forwards raw data.

levels.label: information recognition
levels.evidence: Recognizes states or deviations itself (e.g. condition rules, edge analytics, quality flags).

levels.label: decision ability
levels.evidence: Takes decisions within a defined scope (e.g. self-adjusting parameters, autonomous rescheduling).

levels.label: none
levels.evidence: Location known only by people or fixed by layout.

levels.label: localizable
levels.evidence: Location determined automatically (RFID gates, RTLS, barcode scans at checkpoints, AGV positions).

levels.label: stationary
levels.evidence: Fixed lines and machines.

levels.label: partly mobile
levels.evidence: Equipment or workstations relocated between orders or shifts (mobile carts, modular cells).

levels.label: mobile
levels.evidence: Equipment that moves during operation (AGV/AMR, mobile robots, mobile devices for workers).

levels.label: manual
levels.evidence: Manual operations with tools.

levels.label: partly automated
levels.evidence: Mixed manual and automated steps.

levels.label: fully automated
levels.evidence: Line runs automatically end to end within its scope.

levels.label: modularly automated
levels.evidence: Automation built from standardized modules that can be recombined (plug and produce, MTP-like module concepts).

levels.label: none
levels.evidence: Information comes verbally or not at all.

levels.label: analogous
levels.evidence: Paper, shift boards, printed work instructions.

levels.label: digital (stationary)
levels.evidence: Fixed terminals, line dashboards, andon screens.

levels.label: digital (mobile)
levels.evidence: Tablets, smartphones, wearables with role-based content.

levels.label: augmented / virtual reality
levels.evidence: AR/VR for instructions, maintenance or training.

levels.label: none
levels.evidence: No interaction possible.

levels.label: technical
levels.evidence: Machine panels, SCADA screens, keyboard and mouse.

levels.label: natural
levels.evidence: Voice, gesture, conversational assistants, intuitive touch UIs.

levels.label: none
levels.evidence: No network connection.

levels.label: cable-based
levels.evidence: Wired Ethernet or fieldbus.

levels.label: wireless
levels.evidence: Wi-Fi, private 5G, LPWAN or other wireless links.

levels.label: none
levels.evidence: No data exchange.

levels.label: proprietary
levels.evidence: Vendor-specific protocols and drivers (proprietary PLC protocols, custom file formats).

levels.label: standardized
levels.evidence: Open standards (OPC UA, MQTT, Modbus TCP, EUROMAP 77/83 for injection molding, umati).

levels.label: (4th level - not defined in Table 5)
levels.evidence: Plausibly: standardized plus semantic information models (companion specs, Sparkplug B, AAS submodels). Unconfirmed.

levels.label: none
levels.evidence: No systematic collection.

levels.label: historical
levels.evidence: Data logged and available later (historian exports, batch uploads, daily reports).

levels.label: real-time
levels.evidence: Data available in seconds or less to consumers (streams, subscriptions).

levels.label: none
levels.evidence: No storage.

levels.label: outsourced
levels.evidence: Stored centrally away from the asset (plant server, data center, cloud).

levels.label: combined
levels.evidence: Local buffer or store at asset or edge plus central storage.

levels.label: embedded
levels.evidence: Data stored in the asset or product itself (smart product, device memory, RFID with data).

levels.label: none
levels.evidence: No processing.

levels.label: outsourced
levels.evidence: All logic runs centrally (MES, server, cloud).

levels.label: combined
levels.evidence: Edge pre-processing plus central analytics.

levels.label: embedded
levels.evidence: Processing within the asset (smart sensors, PLC-embedded analytics).

levels.label: none
levels.evidence: No analytics.

levels.label: descriptive
levels.evidence: Reports and dashboards (OEE, scrap rates).

levels.label: diagnostic
levels.evidence: Root-cause analysis, correlations, drill-downs.

levels.label: predictive
levels.evidence: Forecasts and predictions (predictive maintenance, predictive quality).

levels.label: prescriptive
levels.evidence: Recommendations or optimized actions (setpoint optimization, scheduling).

levels.label: no control system
levels.evidence: No systematic control (manual planning).

levels.label: centralized
levels.evidence: Central MES or planning system controls all units.

levels.label: hybrid
levels.evidence: Central planning with local autonomy for defined decisions.

levels.label: decentralized
levels.evidence: Autonomous units negotiate and decide (agent-based, fractal).

levels.label: no continuity
levels.evidence: Each system has its own data model; mapping happens manually or per interface.

levels.label: partly continuous
levels.evidence: Shared models in parts (e.g. common material master, partial naming standards).

levels.label: continuous
levels.evidence: One consistent semantic model across systems and levels - the same asset, order and product mean the same thing everywhere.

a5.name: Variety of warehouses, employees and machines to manage

a7.name: Heterogeneity of customers and customer groups

a14.name: Control and monitoring requirements on the shop floor

a19.name: Consistency of the information flow along the order process

a23.name: Disruptions and outages of production resources

a25.name: Networking of processes and process steps

a27.name: Centralization of planning and control tasks
